title: Oh, But You Digress
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece dissects how digressions quietly sabotage team meetings, distinguishing major digressions that hijack an entire discussion from minor ones that clutter an individual's point with unnecessary asides. The archivist's takeaway: teams that tolerate digression drift lose momentum and disengage participants who are waiting for the actual agenda to resume. Leaders often make things worse by joining in rather than redirecting. The piece argues that naming the pattern out loud and pre-announcing a willingness to interrupt is what separates disciplined teams from meandering ones.
points: Major digressions hijack an entire meeting's purpose; minor digressions bury a speaker's own point in irrelevant detail.
Team members who endure a digression often disengage and struggle to re-enter the discussion afterward.
Leaders sometimes unwittingly worsen digressions by adding their own tangents.
Naming the pattern and warning the team in advance reframes interruptions as supportive rather than rude.
Leaders must actually follow through on interrupting digressions once they've promised to.
quotes: Once a major digression occurs, it is exceedingly hard to put the genie back in the bottle.
As the team patiently endures the digression, what needs to be said and discussed has to wait.
Leaders are expected to do something about this but are often unintentional accomplices by adding their own two cents to the digression.
This advanced notice reframes the interruption from one of impolite interjection to a necessary action to support team progress.
Digressions are the enemy of every meeting and team discussion.
